title: Robust Nonclassical magnon pair generation and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality violation in a hybrid electromagnonic system
authors: Sabur A Barbhuiya, Ajeet Kumar, Amarendra K Sarma
abstract: Magnonic systems are a promising resource for quantum technologies because of their ability to couple significantly disparate quantum platforms and the generation of nonclassical magnon states through magnon blockade has attracted growing attention. In practice, however magnon blockade relies on a destructive interference that is easily spoiled by fabrication-induced coupling asymmetries. Here we show that the relative phase between two magnon drives acts as an active compensation knob that restores this interference even when the couplings are mismatched. We study two Kittel magnon modes in a hybrid system in which a superconducting qubit coupled to a common cavity mode mediates the inter-mode interaction and we find that tuning the drive phase produces both magnon blockade and a strong violation of the classical Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. We derive the analytic condition for the phase that compensates a given coupling asymmetry and confirm it against exact numerical simulations. The drive phase thereby serves as a control knob that switches the system between classical and quantum regimes. Our results enable phase-controlled magnonic quantum information processing.
summary: The paper investigates generating nonclassical magnon pairs in a hybrid electromagnonic circuit by controlling the relative phase of external microwave drives. By tuning this phase, researchers can actively restore destructive interference pathways that suppress single-mode excitations while enhancing cross-mode correlations. This control mechanism allows for robust demonstration of quantum phenomena, such as violating the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, paving the way for phase-controlled magnonic quantum information processing.
main_problem: The study aims to achieve robust nonclassical magnon pair generation and demonstrate violation of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality by actively controlling quantum interference in a hybrid electromagnonic system.
main_result: The relative drive phase acts as a dynamic control knob, enabling the simultaneous achievement of strong blockade and unambiguous violation of the macroscopic CSI ($R \gg 1$).
method: The dynamics are analyzed using numerical solutions to the Lindblad master equation, supplemented by perturbative expansions in coupling strengths.
model_or_system: The system is a tripartite hybrid quantum setup involving two Kittel magnon modes ($	ext{M}_1, 	ext{M}_2$) coupled via a common microwave cavity bus and mediated by a superconducting qubit. The effective Hamiltonian is derived after adiabatically eliminating the cavity mode.
key_observables: Second-order autocorrelation functions ($g^{(2)}_{aa}(0)$) and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality violation factor ($R = g^{(2)}_{12}(0)/\sqrt{g^{(2)}_{11}(0)g^{(2)}_{22}(0)}$).
important_parameters: The relative drive phase ($\phi$) is the key control parameter, alongside coupling ratios and detunings.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on operating in the large detuning (dispersive) limit to adiabatically eliminate the cavity mode, which was validated by comparing effective vs. exact dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how varying the drive phase ($\phi$) controls interference pathways, leading to high values of $R$ (up to 73.4) at optimal phases like $\phi^* \simeq 1.18\pi$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and uses perturbative methods to derive amplitudes ($C_{g...}$) showing phase dependence, then numerically solves the master equation to quantify nonclassicality via $R$, and finally validates the effective Hamiltonian approach against exact time evolution.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum control in coupled bosonic systems (magnons), using external driving fields ($\phi$) as a knob to switch between classical and highly correlated quantum regimes, which is central to quantum optics and open quantum system research.
